document: Restrict post-2021 migrants from acquiring Indefinite Leave to Remain, We urge the Government to severely restrict the right to obtain ILR for migrants who came to the UK after 2021. We believe the exact requirements to claim ILR should be reviewed, so that only a small minority of migrants who arrived after 2021 can permanently stay in the UK., We believe the number of recent arrivals since 2021 is too large and is placing unsustainable pressure on UK housing and public services. We believe only a minority of the most valuable post-2021 migrants should get the right to ILR in the UK.

Require hunting hounds to wear muzzles when on a trail or clean boot hunt, We ask that the government bring in a new law which requires mandatory wearing of humane, approved muzzles, such as basket muzzles, by all fox hunting hounds when trail or clean boot hunting. Basket muzzles made from rubber plastic or metal allow dogs to drink, breathe & pant. , In the trail hunting process foxes may still be caught & killed due to the hounds being in fox habitat.
Foxes, other wildlife, farm animals & domestic pets may be hurt & killed. We think this can be avoided by a legal requirement that all hunting hounds must wear muzzles when on a hunt.

Abolish Vehicle Excise Duty and add the cost to Fuel Duty, I would like Vehicle Excise Duty (VED) to be completely abolished. Instead, add the cost to Fuel Duty. I think this will mean that for more fuel-efficient vehicles which generally use less fuel and emit less CO2, drivers will pay less for fuel, and this change may help wider zero carbon policies., Older, less efficient vehicles can disappear naturally without some families potentially feeling forced into rash decisions about vehicle use.
 
In my view, any attempt to fast-track carbon reduction by hiking certain taxes like VED may make the country poorer. I think the infrastructure needed to do the things government wants to do is decades behind. I believe that it should be the case that the more fuel you use, the more tax you pay.

Reform the British Spouse Visa System, Many British citizens and their spouses face huge costs, with the initial visa application costing £4,951(including the healthcare surcharge), the extension application priced at £3,845.50, and the settlement (ILR) application at £2,885. Over five years, families may have to pay more than £11,000., I do not believe family unity should not come with an exorbitant price tag. I believe the current system places undue stress on families, penalising them for seeking the simple right to live together. I think reforming the spouse visa process is essential to uphold fairness, equality, and compassion in the UK’s immigration policies. I believe Ireland’s Spouse Immigration System offers a model of fairness and compassion. Spouses of Irish citizens are exempt from visa fees.

End the Immigration Health Surcharge for National Insurance payers, People may be struggling to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge, when they are renewing their residence permits. If they are working and paying national insurance and taxes, we think it's not fair that people have to then pay again for the Health Service Charge when they apply to renew their visa., I want the Government to end the Immigration Health Surcharge for those who are working and contributing towards national insurance and taxes. Because there are people who are struggling and under pressure, but also immigrants doing well to support the country.

Make the carrying of ID cards mandatory, We are concerned about reports on the numbers of illegal immigrants in the country. We think that mandatory ID cards should now be introduced as a matter of urgency to identify who has a right to be here legally.,

Create a visa route for Palestinian Orphans and Simplify Adoption Processes, We think the Government should establish a clear and accessible process for bringing orphaned babies to the UK, ensuring that prospective adoptive parents, charities, or other responsible entities can apply for visas on their behalf. , We think consideration should also be given to setting a specific number or percentage of orphaned babies eligible to come to the UK to provide clarity and direction.
 
We think Palestinian orphans are facing a severe crisis after losing their parents in conflict, leaving them vulnerable and without stability. We think the UK has an opportunity to help by facilitating their adoption, reflecting its values of compassion and responsibility. We think this action would address an urgent humanitarian need, uphold children's rights, and promote global solidarity. By providing these children with a safe home, we think the UK can offer them a chance to rebuild their lives and contribute to society.

Allow ICT (intracompany transfer) visas to count towards ILR, We feel that there are many people living in the UK that love the country and have paid taxes, but cannot stay permanently without sponsorship because ICT visas do not count towards Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR). , We want the Government to change this and allow all former ICT visa holders to have the time spent working in the UK to contribute to their ILR.

We feel that the Government has already made these people go through strict immigration processes to qualify for ICT and that this shows individuals' suitability to qualify for ILR.

We feel that changing this would help many people that have done their time to stay in the UK and continue to contribute without having the added stress of an even longer wait time for ILR.

Retain the UK's stockpile of Plutonium and make more, I want the government to retain the current stockpile of plutonium and ensure it is used to fuel nuclear power stations in future. I think that to bury it now might save storage costs short term, but it would no longer be available for future use., Plutonium is made from Uranium 238 in nuclear reactors. It is itself, a fuel to produce more power. I think that if the UK's stock of existing spent fuel rods were processed to make more Plutonium, it could power future reactors and we would have enough power to supply the UK for generations to come.

Close the borders and start a program of mass deportation of illegal migrants, The new USA Trump administration has started mass deportation of illegal immigrants. Hopefully they will deport as many as President Obama who deported 3 million such people. The German government has voted to close the borders to illegal migrants. We should follow these good examples.,

Stop benefits and free healthcare for immigrants who have not worked in the UK, I urge the Government to prevent all immigrants who have not worked and paid UK tax & national insurance in the UK for a minimum of 5 years, from accessing benefits and free healthcare., I believe this will benefit the U.K. massively in economic terms. It could help stop people living off the state, which I believe is out of control, unsustainable and is the intention of many people who come to the UK.

Illegal immigrants should not have a path to UK citizenship., We do not want Illegal Immigration Act 2023 repealed by the Border Security Bill. 

Specifically those measures contained within it that protect U.K. citizens and legal immigrants., It is the Governments first duty to protect its citizens and those who are here legally.

The changes proposed will encourage the gangs and not ‘smash’ them. The removal of scientific age assessment tests will put school children and foster parents at risk.

More people will die making the crossing if they are incentivised by citizenship and the privileges that affords them. 

Becoming a U.K. citizenship should be a privilege and not a right gained through illegal means.

Demand Government reverse their decision to postpone local elections for a year, We want all these local elections to go ahead this year.
Any extension of term of office should be approved by the local electorate and this has not been. His Majesty the King should not approve this undemocratic measure.
Any proposed reorganisation of local councils should have a local referendum, The government must allow these local elections to take place even if some Councillors have a potential short term of office.
The government want to create super local authorities each covering about 500,000 people.
This could result in less local power and more centralised power.
These proposals may not happen as there may not be agreement or local voters may decide against them in a referendum.
Such proposals should not be dictated but decided by local referenda,
which should be organised.

End the Injustice: Grant British Nationals (Overseas) Full UK Citizenship, We want the government to address what we feel is a long-standing injustice and grant BN(O)s full citizenship rights we think they deserve. We think this would be a recognition of their historical ties to the UK and also a reaffirmation of the UK's commitment to democratic principles & human rights., Hong Kong's 1997 handover to China lacked a referendum, denying its people self-determination. We think this undemocratic act was worsened by refusing BN(O)s full UK citizenship, a right we think they deserved as former British subjects. The BN(O) visa offers residency and a path to citizenship, but we think it doesn't correct this historical injustice. We think BN(O)s, under British colonial rule, should have the same rights as any British citizen.
 
We believe this would uphold the principles of democracy and human rights by correcting historical wrongs and ending inequality.

Remove visa requirements for non-UK spouses of UK citizens to visit the UK, We urge the Government to remove visa requirements for non-UK spouses of British citizens when they come to visit the UK, such as for a short stay with family. We feel that the cost of visas for non-UK spouses often outweighs the cost of travel., We believe the spouse of an overseas Brit travelling with that Brit to visit family or to have a vacation should be able to travel freely with their British spouse. We believe that to prohibit such movement seems to be denying families the right to gather together.

2-year ILR spouse visa route for all long-term residents on prior visas , Create a faster ILR pathway for those in the UK 3+ years (e.g., student/work visas) marrying British citizens and entered the UK after 2012. Allow ILR after 2 years on a spouse visa, not 5. Require marriage to a British citizen (by birth or naturalised ≥10 years) and proof of integration., We think current rules unfairly treat long-term residents like new arrivals, ignoring prior contributions (taxes, NHS fees, integration). We think a 2-year spouse visa route for those who arrived post 2012 but have been here 3+ years would reward commitment, reduce financial/emotional strain, and keep families together. We think it would target a small group without undermining immigration controls. We think personal cases, like mine, show penalising integration after years of study/work, fluency, and marriage to a British citizen is unfair. We think this aligns with UK values of rewarding contribution and family unity.

Reverse guidance stopping refugees gaining citizenship, The 'Nationality: good character requirement' guidance was updated on 10 February 2025, preventing many refugees from ever becoming British citizens. We urge ministers to urgently reverse this policy or update the guidance to confirm refugees are exempt., The guidance states that anyone who entered the UK illegally/having made a dangerous journey will “normally” be refused British citizenship.

Many refugees who entered the UK through irregular means will therefore be prevented from ever becoming British - no matter how long they live in the UK or the contributions they make.

We believe this policy breaches Article 31 and Article 34 of the Refugee Convention.

Shut the migrant hotels down now and deport illegal migrants housed there, The Labour Party pledged to end asylum hotels if it won power. Labour is now in power.
, It has transpired that the migrant hotels may stay open for at least the next 4 years.
 
We want to see the migrant hotels shut down now and all illegal migrants housed in them deported immediately.

Update on consultation on Overseas Dentist Provisional Registration Route, We urge the UK Government to publish the responses and next steps to the consultation on overseas dentist provisional registration route. The consultation closed in May. We think the Govt must clarify why progress stalled, provide a clear timeline, and prioritize resolving NHS dental shortages., We think the NHS faces a catastrophic dental care crisis, with many unable to access treatment and vulnerable patients suffering preventable pain. We think the provisional registration route proposed for qualified overseas dentists as an alternative to the ORE exam could immediately alleviate shortages. Yet, despite a consultation closing in 2024, there is no update. We think delays worsen the crisis: A 2022 study showed that 90% of UK practices refuse new adult NHS patients.

We think the new government must clarify why this solution remains stalled.

Funding for Hyperemesis Gravidarum care, We call on the UK Government to provide funding to improve physical and mental healthcare for sufferers, increase training, eliminate inequities in access and treatment as well as ensure HG sufferers have access to mental health support within 2 weeks of referral., Up to 30,000 people will suffer with HG in 2025, all 8 times more likely to develop antenatal depression than other pregnant people. Hyperemesis gravidarum is not “morning sickness”—it is a debilitating pregnancy condition that profoundly impacts physical and mental health. For too long, we feel the suffering of women with HG has been dismissed. We feel HG sufferers remain excluded from the services they desperately need.

Add Biomedical Scientists to the immigration salary list, Recognise Biomedical Scientists as a shortage occupation and adjust immigration rules. Add them to the immigration salary list to lower salary thresholds for visa extensions., We think Biomedical Scientists are essential for diagnosing diseases, including cancer and infections. The NHS faces a severe shortage, yet we think current immigration rules force many to leave due to salary thresholds. We think losing these professionals worsens diagnostic delays and strains healthcare services. Therefore retaining them could be crucial for patient care and NHS sustainability

Illegal immigrants entering this country to have DNA taken, We think it should be mandatory for illegal immigrants entering this country to have their DNA taken., Often no one knows who these people are, so I think at the very least their DNA should be taken.
 
People who are arrested in this country have their DNA taken.

Support the proposed International Treaty to Ban the Political Abuse of Religion, We urge the Government to support the proposed ‘International Treaty to Ban the Political Abuse of Religion’, which we believe would be a crucial foundation to eliminate the root causes of religious conflicts and discrimination, especially against women, children and religious minorities., We believe this proposed treaty could touch the lives of billions because we think it would eliminate the root causes of many conflicts and a long list of violations of human rights. We believe it could create functioning societies and enhance stability worldwide.

Introduce a 12-month amnesty on APR and BPR policy proposals, Introduce a 12-month amnesty, as we think it would allow for the transfer of land & chattels of agricultural businesses to a named person before changes to Agricultural Property Relief (APR) and Business Property Relief (BPR) are made., We think it would remove what is, in our view, the negative human impact of the policy changes in the Autumn Budget 2024. We believe the tax change proposals within the Budget could be creating torment for farming families and that some ageing farmers could be feeling a burden to their successors.
 
We believe introducing this limited protection would help those affected arrange their affairs and provide an opportunity for government to address what is, in our view, a devastating policy proposal.

Require local authorities to add "unmet needs" as a Child Protection category, Families seeking support for a disabled child can end up going through child protection routes. When a local authority issues a child protection plan, professionals working with the family have to assign one of five categories e.g. physical abuse, sexual abuse, emotional abuse, neglect or multiple. , We think these categories assign parent blame and therefore want a new category "unmet needs".

When parents of children with disabilities (CWD) seek help, they can end up on a safeguarding pathway. The minimum criteria for a CWD Social Worker (SW) is high e.g. must have autism and a learning difficulty, which can result in families being assigned SW's with safeguarding as their primary training, rather than disabilities. These families can get trapped in a safeguarding loop which we feel breaks down trust and currently, if placed on Child Protection, this can have lifelong DBS consequences including loss of work. We want change.

Ban all UK economic & charitable activities with all illegal settlements, We call on the Government to bring forth legislation that will prohibit all economic and charitable activities, including any trade and investment, with any illegal settlement in territories deemed occupied under international law., Successive UK governments have held the position that settlements in territories deemed occupied under international law are illegal. We believe such settlement enterprises entail serious breaches of peremptory norms of international law. We believe the UK’s failure to ban all trade and investment activities by UK-based businesses with illegal settlements could be contrary to the UK’s obligated duties under international law.

EU WORKING VISA for uk citizens for contractors/self employed, EU work visa that UK offshore workers can apply for without employer sponsorship. The existing visa routes require either a job offer or high-level qualifications, making it difficult for UK offshore workers, self-employed contractors, or temporary workers to access legal employment in the EU, Simplified Self-Employed or Contractor Visa with EU or individual countries or introduce a freelancer/contractor visa that does not require a sponsor. This could work similarly to digital nomad visas but would allow short-term work in regulated industries for offshore workers 

UK and EU could negotiate a sector-specific agreement for offshore workers, allowing temporary work permits

Allow Dependents (Esp. those in the UK) Under the Care Worker Visa (SOC 6135)., We indulge the Government to reconsider&amend the policy on dependents in the UK from the Visa. It creates significant emotional, social, &practical hardships for us, ultimately affecting our ability to provide High-Quality Care, Worker Retention, & causing Family Separation, Emotional Strain,, We respectfully call on the UK Government to
*Allow dependents of H&C worker visa holders(SOC 6135) stay with them in the UK
*Recognise the importance of family unity & its role in the mental wellbeing of care workers
*Acknowledge the positive impact that supporting families will have on care worker retention & the quality of care provided
*Prioritise the wellbeing of care workers & their families, recognising that happy & healthy workforce is essential for the success of UK’s healthcare system

Give conditional amnesty to undocumented migrants living in the UK for 10+ years, We urge the Government to grant conditional amnesty to undocumented migrants who have lived in the UK for over 10 years, on the condition that they pay a financial penalty (e.g., £10,000), mandatory tax contributions, and have no access to public benefits for 10 years., This is to ensure they contribute to society while their status is regularised. Deporting undocumented migrants can cost the UK millions of pounds. We believe a conditional amnesty policy would generate revenue through fines and taxes. By doing this, legalised individuals can pay into the system instead of working illegally. This proposal could lead to economic benefits while discouraging future illegal immigration through a strict eligibility criteria.

End the construction of the mega mosque in the lake District., Stop the construction of the lake District mega mosque. This is destroying the wildlife and natural beauty for no reason whatsoever. It is not needed.,

Repeal the Human Rights Act 1998, We urge the Government to repeal the Human Rights Act 1998. We believe this would allow the UK to create a tougher deterrence to protect British borders and help stop illegal migration., We believe we must stop illegal immigration, as we think it is having a tremendous influence on Britain, British nationals and communities. We want to create a safe country that upholds its values and laws not based on religion but on its history. We think the Government needs to be tougher and to deal with illegal immigration to the UK.

Cap the Indefinite Leave to Remain fee at £3000 , We feel that increasing ILR fees risk financial hardship for families as they must save for the fee with the high cost of living. We want the Government to consider the value people with visas bring to the economy. We believe the UK is losing valued people because of increasingly high fees., We want the fee to be capped because increasing ILR fees may bring financial hardship particularly for families and workers from different countries who have incurred substantial expenses securing ancestry visas and family based visas etc. This may necessitate immigrants to return to their country of origin because they cannot afford the demands of the increasingly high ILR fees. We feel both applicants and the UK lose the investments made if this happens.

Tag and trace all illegal immigrants, We believe the Government response to illegal immigration has been weak. We are concerned about the illegal immigration and the lack of information about past criminal activity of some illegal immigrants in their native country. We believe enough is enough!, We urge the Government to implement a "Tag and Track" system for illegal immigrants. Many UK citizens are concerned about the impact of illegal immigration on communities and resources and how their taxes may support illegal entrants. We propose electronic monitoring to ensure compliance with immigration laws and which includes monitoring locations and real-time data. We think the proposal will ensure public safety and a system to address illegal immigration and protect citizens' rights.

Donate migrant boats to emergency services and volunteer rescue teams, We urge the Government to donate confiscated migrant boats to emergency services and rescue teams, even damaged ones - which can be used in training scenarios, instead of putting them into costly storage., We believe this will reduce costs of storage and could mean emergency services and volunteer services have access to invaluable resources, especially during major incidents like flooding.

Base childcare support for working parents on household income, We suggest basing eligibility for childcare support for working parents on household income, rather than individual income., Compare these two families under the current rules:
Family A) Two parents each earning £95k = £190k total household income → 30 free childcare hours
Family B) One parent earning £105k, the other £40k = £145k total household income → no childcare help

We believe that this isn’t just illogical — it’s unjust. We think it risks trapping many parents (mostly mothers) in unemployment, as without any support, childcare costs can exceed their income — all because one parent earns "too much."

Add checkpoints on the border between Ireland & Northern Ireland, We urge the government to add checkpoints with border patrol between Ireland & Northern Ireland. By adding checkpoints, we think the Government could manage cross-border movement, prevent illegal activities and people illegally crossing. We want the government to take immediate action on this issue, For a decade, the open border between Ireland and N, Ireland has allowed for the free movement of citizens. However, we think this policy has been exploited, leading to a surge in illegal immigration. We think the unchecked of individuals across the border has contributed to rising public violence and unrest, that threaten the safety of our communities. We believe that the government should take action to this situation by adding reinstating checkpoints.

Allow BNO students in the process of getting ILR to apply as home students, We urge the Government to ensure that BNO Visa students who will have Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) before the start of their university course are eligible to apply as home students when submitting applications through UCAS., Currently, candidates who are due to obtain ILR before their course begins in September must still apply via the overseas student route if their ILR is not yet granted at the time of application. We feel this results in unfair treatment and may affect their chances of securing offers. We believe this policy should be updated to ensure fairness and equal opportunity for all applicants.

Remove IT and related roles eligibility for the skilled worker visa, We urge the Government to remove IT and related roles eligibility for the skilled worker visa to prioritize employment opportunities for UK-based IT professionals., We think skilled IT professionals in the UK may be struggling to find employment. We think continuing to list IT roles as shortage occupations undermines local talent and does not reflect the current job market.

Call for Fair Graduate Route  Visa Decisions End Inconsistent Home Office Policy, Govt. Must ensure consistent Graduate visa decisions by formally recognising lawful variation from FLR under Section 3C. Discretion should apply where delays are beyond students’ control, especially late award reporting. Clear guidance is needed for caseworkers & universities must report awards., Govt.& the Home Office should change their policy to uphold fairness, legal consistency & the UK’s reputation.  The Home Office is failing to apply its own rules consistently, while universities delay reporting awards issues beyond students’ control. This results in injustice, uncertainty, and loss of future opportunities for graduates. It undermines confidence in the UK’s immigration system and deters future international students.It affects UK Int'l market not suitable for naitonal interest.

Review SWE processes & the Fitness to Practice guidance, Review the Fitness to Practice processes, to ensure staff are adequately trained, reduce the volume of cases passed to case examiners, ensure hearings are kept for those whose fitness to practice is actually impaired. We think this would reduce timescales and reducing costs to social workers and SWE, Social Work England was established 5 years ago, and we think the situation for any social worker referred to SWE is dire. We feel staff at initial stages may be untrained/unskilled in making ethical assessments and have little to no knowledge of our role. We think cases may be wrongly assessed adding to the delays. We feel social workers may be left unable to work when cases are being investigated, having life changing impacts. We think SWE's answer is to increase our fees by 1/3 to pay for more legal outsourcing, which is not the answer.

Create an Open Work Visa for Skilled Workers after 3 years, We ask the Government to introduce an Open Work Visa for those on the Skilled Worker visa, after 3 years, with the ability to renew yearly until ILR eligibility. We believe this could improve mobility, reduce exploitation, and allow skilled workers to contribute more fully to the UK economy., The Skilled Worker Visa ties employees to one sponsor for 5 years, limiting mobility. Finding a new sponsor can be hard, and we believe that some employers exploit this by underpaying or overworking staff. This can lead to workers missing better roles and employers without a licence can’t hire them. We feel the Global Talent Visa offers flexibility only to a few. We believe an Open Work Visa after 3 years, with yearly renewal until ILR, could reduce exploitation, promote fairness, and boost skilled workers’ contribution to the UK economy.

Exempt employed British passport holders from paying income tax, We want the Government to exempt employed British passport holders from paying income tax, We think it is unfair that we work so hard each day and have to pay large proportion of our wages in taxes each month. We think current policy is causing a lot of people to struggle to survive in the UK.

Proposal to remove from Office The Prime Minister Keir Starmer., Proposal to remove from Office Prime Minister Keir Starmer who’s policies are and have seriously undermined the successful administration of this country.,

Skilled worker visa holders & UK taxpayers eligible for Childcare Benefits, We, the undersigned, urge the UK Government to extend eligibility for childcare benefits—including Child Benefit, 30 hours of free childcare, and Tax-Free Childcare—to all skilled workers and taxpayers residing in the UK, irrespective of their immigration status., We propose that the UK Government:
 
Amend current policies to allow individuals on Skilled Worker visas access to Child Benefit, 30 hours of free childcare, and Tax-Free Childcare, provided they meet the standard eligibility criteria unrelated to immigration status.
 
Recognize the contributions of skilled workers to the UK economy and public services by ensuring equitable access to childcare support, thereby promoting workforce participation and child development.

Introduce a Minister for Deportations at the Home Office, Introduce a dedicated Minister for Deportations at the Home Office, with their own team and budget, focused solely on deportations., We believe our borders are out of control, that the volume of immigration is unsustainable, and that we need tough and decisive action.
We have had enough of what is, in our view, the Government's failure to deal with legal and illegal immigration.
We think we need a dedicated Minister for Deportations who will work solely in this area of Home Office policy.

Fund off-road cycle paths linking every village, town and city in the country, We want the government to fund and construct a network of off-road cycle paths linking every town, village and city in the country., We think the construction of these paths will allow all short distance journeys to be cycled safely. We also think this will reduce traffic on the roads for those who need to use them.

Declare a national emergency due to the uncontrolled illegal immigration, I want parliament to declare a national emergency to put an immediate stop to the uncontrolled illegal immigration ongoing, The country is being used for its goodwill, benefits, housing, dental and medical care which is costing the ordinary hard working citizens and lower their standard of living.

Ban the use of audible propane bird scarers, We think audible propane bird scarers, known as gas gun bird scarers, should be banned due to their disruptive nature. While used by farmers to scare birds away, we feel they cause significant noise pollution, disturbing residents, animals, and passers by., We also think their effectiveness is questionable because birds frequently return. We think these devices could harm wildlife and pose safety risks, yet remain largely unregulated. Despite their limited effectiveness, only non-binding National Farmers Union guidance exists. We call for a ban to help safeguard residents, animals, and the environment.

Keep the 5-Year ILR pathway for existing Skilled Worker visa holders, Do not apply the proposed 10-year ILR rule to existing Skilled Worker visa holders. Keep the 5-year ILR route for those already in the UK on this visa. Apply any changes only to new applicants from the date of implementation., Many skilled visa holders moved to the UK for better opportunities and in return have contributed to the UK economy, paid taxes, and supported critical sectors like health, care, and engineering. We think that changing ILR rules mid-journey is unfair and causes stress for families. Apply the 10-year rule only to future Skilled Worker entrants, not those already building a life here under the current system.

Protect Legal Migrants: do not implement the 10-Year ILR proposal, We urge the UK Government to scrap plans to extend ILR from 5 to 10 years. We feel that legal migrants, especially care workers, followed the rules and built lives here under the 5-year promise. We think they support vital services and deserve fairness, not shifting rules., We think that retroactively extending ILR from 5 to 10 years is unfair. We are concerned that it creates insecurity for legal migrants, disrupts vital sectors like health and care, and adds financial strain. We urge the UK Government to withdraw this proposal, protect visa renewals, and prioritise tackling illegal migration. Do not penalise those who follow the law, support the economy, and uphold British values. We think legal migration must be protected, not discouraged.

Exempt existing skilled worker from Increasing ILR time from 5 to 10 years, Exempt existing skilled worker from Increasing settlement and citizenship time from 5 to 10 years Or clarify if its already considered as exemption in submission of white paper, Because existing skilled workers are here based on existing rules and regulations

Do not change ILR qualification period, PSW duration for existing immigrants., The recent proposal to increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years should not be changed from the current 5 years and PSW duration should not be reduced from 24 months to 18 years. All other proposed changes in immigration system white paper should not be for Legal existing immigrants., Retroactively applying new immigration rules to existing immigrants violates the principle of legal certainty. These individuals made life-altering decisions based on current policies, investing in homes,careers, and communities under a legitimate expectation of stability. Changing requirements midway creates severe hardship, disrupting established lives and breaking implicit social contracts. It undermines trust in government, UK's international reputation and contradicts fundamental principles

Defend legal immigration: Keep ILR to 5 years for existing skilled workers, The Labour Government has announced plans to increase the settlement period required for ILR - from 5 to 10 years. This drastic change delays the path to permanent residency for many people who built their lives in the UK. We urge the government to reconsider this proposal and provide clear guidance,

Current Skilled Worker visa holders should remain on the 5yrs ILR path not 10yrs, We urge the Government to ensure that current Skilled Worker and Health Care visa holders on the 5-year ILR route are not affected by the new 10-year rule. They should continue on the original 5-year path to ILR as promised when they first moved to the UK., We want the Government to honor the commitment made to current Skilled Worker and Health Care visa holders. These individuals have been contributing to the UK economy, especially during the pandemic. Changing the rules mid-way would be unfair, causing uncertainty and hardship for those who have made long-term plans based on the 5-year ILR path. It is essential that these workers can continue their journey to ILR as originally promised, ensuring fairness and stability in the immigration system.

Allow licences to be issued to wildlife rehabilitators to release grey squirrels, We ask the Government to amend the Invasive Alien Species (Enforcement and Permitting) Order 2019 to allow Natural England to issue licences to wildlife rehabilitators to release rehabilitated grey squirrels., We believe the current law criminalises compassionate wildlife care and does not affect the grey squirrel population, already well established in the UK.

Some estimates suggest there are around 2.5 to 3 million grey squirrels in the UK. We think preventing the release of a small number of rehabilitated individuals by wildlife carers does not materially reduce their numbers but imposes, in our view, unnecessary penalties on those trying to help injured or orphaned animals.

We believe our proposal would remove what we see as a perverse disincentive on veterinary and conservation practitioners, without advancing the species’ spread and without compromising biosecurity objectives.

Keep existing skilled worker visa holders’ 5 year route to settlement, We ask that Home Office confirms in writing to retain the existing five-year route to settlement for all Skilled Worker visa holders, and commit to no further extensions of the qualifying period., Extending the settlement route obliterates economic stability—businesses, academia, and NHS depend on a guaranteed five-year path to retain talent. In 2006, shifting from 4 to 5 years to ILR for HSMP holders caused critical controversy and was deemed illegal by the High Court. Skilled workers bought homes, invested, paid taxes, and built communities under the five-year promise; changing this now breaks trust, burdens employers and families, inflates costs, and tarnishes the UK’s global standing.

Grandfather existing applicants under 5-year ILR rules, With the release of the “Restoring Control Over Immigration” white paper, many UK residents are now facing uncertainty and unnecessary hardship due to extended ILR requirements. We urge the government not to apply these proposed rules to those on the current 5-year path., We urge the government to consider applying a grandfather clause to legal residents on the current 5-year ILR path. Residents who began this path made life decisions based on existing rules. Changing requirements mid-way undermines trust despite compliance with current laws. Many affected individuals have lived, worked, paid taxes, and raised families in the UK for years. The UK has used grandfather clauses before to protect those affected by policy shifts.

Ensure that immigrants on existing visas remain on the 5-year path to ILR., The UK government plans to extend the wait time for eligibility for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR) from 5 years to 10 years. Please ensure that immigrants on existing visas remain subject to the original 5-year path to ILR; the terms they accepted, when they paid their visa fees and NHS subcharge., UK laws must not be retrospective. Immigrants on existing visas have paid substantial sums of money in visa application fees and NHS subcharges, as well as made significant life-changing decisions to migrate here, with the original 5-year path to ILR in mind. If the UK government fails to preserve these terms they agreed to, then this is a retrospective application of the law, which is unfair, exploitative and essentially a rug-pull and cash-grab of people in an already difficult situation.

We ask that the 10-year ILR rule not be applied retrospectively., We urge the Government not to apply the 10-year ILR rule retrospectively. Skilled Workers came under a 5-year promise and planned their lives accordingly. Changing rules mid-way is unfair, disrupts families, and breaks trust.
